parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calcium carbide, $\text{CaC}_2$, reacts readily with water, forming ethyne, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$, and a sparingly soluble white ionic compound.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction of $\text{CaC}_2$ with water.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Draw a 'dot-and-cross' diagram for the carbide ion, $\text{C}_2^{2-}$. Show outer electrons only.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Ethyne is the simplest member of the alkyne homologous series.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

Propyne, $\text{C}_3\text{H}_4$, and butyne, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_6$, are the next two members of the series.

Deduce the general formula for the alkynes.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem:
Ethyne can be polymerised into poly(acetylene), which is a conducting polymer.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Suggest why this polymer conducts electricity.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: State the empirical formula of poly(acetylene).

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: By reference to a physical or chemical property, suggest **one** advantage of a conducting polymer when compared with metals.
